name: Linked-data and semantic-web DPP implementation (JSON-LD, RDF, OWL, SHACL, SAMM, vocabularies, knowledge graphs, Solid)
scope_note: Covers DPPs whose data meaning is carried by RDF semantics: JSON-LD 1.1 documents with @context, RDF graphs and their serializations, OWL ontologies and SKOS code lists (CIRPASS-2 EU DPP CORE and sector ontologies, GS1 Web Vocabulary, schema.org, UNTP context, QUDT, UN/CEFACT Rec 20 units), SHACL shapes as validation and access-view specifications, the Eclipse SAMM meta model as used by the Battery Pass data model, LinkML-generated artifacts (CE-RISE), DCAT/DCAT-AP metadata, Linked Data Platform, Solid and the W3C Linked Web Storage drafts, RDF Dataset Canonicalization and VC Data Integrity as they touch integrity. It also covers validation tooling (pySHACL, rdflib, PyLD, jsonld.js, Titanium, Apache Jena SHACL, TopBraid SHACL, the EC ITB SHACL validator, the CIRPASS-2 dpp-validator, CE-RISE DP-AWB). Left out: AAS internals (method aas-digital-twin), GS1 resolver internals beyond linkset media types (web-resolver-gs1), VC/SSI trust frameworks (verifiable-credentials-ssi), EPCIS event semantics (event-traceability-epcis). Protected EN/ISO/IEC/DIN documents appear only as bibliographic metadata. No live DPP system, resolver, SPARQL endpoint, Solid pod, registry or test environment was contacted; only specifications, repositories, package indexes and paper metadata were read.
summary: In this family a passport is a set of RDF statements about a product and its passport record, identified by HTTP(S) IRIs and usually serialized as JSON-LD 1.1, sometimes as Turtle or N-Quads. A JSON-LD @context maps every JSON key to an IRI in a shared vocabulary or ontology, for example the CIRPASS-2 EU DPP CORE ontology (namespace https://w3id.org/eudpp#) with sector modules for batteries, tyres and textiles, the GS1 Web Vocabulary 1.16, schema.org, the UNTP 0.7.0 context, QUDT units or UN/CEFACT Rec 20 unit codes. Constraints are written as SHACL shapes and are checked on the RDF graph that JSON-LD expansion and RDF conversion produce, not on the JSON tree; CIRPASS-2 also uses SHACL view shapes to state what a public, legitimate-interest or authority view must carry and must not disclose. A second variant, Eclipse SAMM, keeps the semantics in an RDF/Turtle aspect model and generates JSON Schema, OpenAPI and sample payloads; the Battery Pass model v1.2.0 follows it, so its instance payloads are plain JSON tied to the model only by a URN. A third variant, LinkML (CE-RISE), generates JSON Schema, OWL and SHACL from one YAML source, and a service resolves these artifacts from a versioned catalog at validation time. End to end, a data carrier holds an HTTP URI such as a GS1 Digital Link; a web server or GS1-conformant resolver answers with content negotiation (application/ld+json, text/turtle, text/html) or with a linkset that can contain the gs1:dpp link type; the client loads the referenced contexts, expands the document to RDF, validates it against pinned shapes and may verify a Data Integrity proof that uses RDF Dataset Canonicalization (RDFC-1.0). Storage ranges from document stores that serve JSON-LD to triplestores with SPARQL and LDP/Solid pods with WAC or ACP access control. EU law names none of RDF, JSON-LD, OWL or SHACL; it requires open-standard, interoperable, machine-readable, structured and searchable passport data (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(d); Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(5)), and the registry act requires passports to follow common versioned data models held in a Commission semantic repository whose metadata conforms to DCAT-AP, with a semantic conformity check at registration (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(7)(a), Art. 11, Art. 12). For a black-box conformance engine the method is attractive because SHACL gives a declarative, inspectable oracle, but determinism needs pinned contexts, pinned shapes, a frozen document loader, a fixed inference mode and pinned processor versions. The main hazards found are silent remote-context loading in common parsers, JSON number typing that turns fractional numbers into xsd:double, namespace variants that defeat class targeting without reasoning, terms that expansion drops without error, and vacuous conformance when no focus node matches. The engine today covers only the context allowlist (data.context); data.shacl is interface_only and integrity covers JOSE only.

maturity.spec_status: The core W3C stack is stable: JSON-LD 1.1 and its API (Recommendations, 16 July 2020), SHACL (Recommendation, 20 July 2017), OWL 2 Second Edition (Recommendation, 11 December 2012), LDP 1.0 (Recommendation, 26 February 2015), DCAT 3 (Recommendation, 22 August 2024), RDF Dataset Canonicalization RDFC-1.0 (Recommendation, 21 May 2024) and VC Data Integrity 1.0 (Recommendation, 15 May 2025). Successor work is in progress and not final: RDF 1.2 Concepts is a Candidate Recommendation Snapshot (7 April 2026), SHACL 1.2 Core is a Working Draft (14 October 2026), Content Negotiation by Profile is a Working Draft (21 September 2026), and Linked Web Storage Protocol 1.0 is a Working Draft (16 October 2026). The Solid Protocol 0.11.0 is a Draft Community Group Report, not on the W3C standards track. DPP-specific ontologies are drafts: CIRPASS-2 CORE 2.0.7 with modules, battery ontology 0.4.0 DRAFT, all with a disclaimer that they are not official. SAMM 2.2.0 is released; Battery Pass v1.2.0 is unmaintained and marked draft by its authors.

maturity.adoption_evidence: Public, inspectable DPP artifacts of this family exist mainly in EU research projects: CIRPASS-2 publishes Apache-2.0 OWL/Turtle ontologies, SHACL shapes, worked examples and a pySHACL test script for batteries, plus a Java validation service (Jena SHACL, Titanium JSON-LD) that accepts JSON-LD payloads; CE-RISE publishes LinkML models, a SHACL-based model assessment workbench and a validation core; the Battery Pass project published SAMM aspect models with generated JSON Schema. GS1 added a gs1:dpp link type to its Web Vocabulary. The literature from 2024 to 2026 is dominated by ontology proposals and small prototypes (CIRPASS-2 CORE critiques, RePlanIT for ICT, an ontology network with SHACL, EPCIS 2.0 plus knowledge graph, a SHACL-based explainable validation prototype); reviews report few empirical, multi-organisation validations. No production DPP system that publishes passports as linked data with SHACL validation was located, and no Solid-pod DPP prototype was located.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: No EU act retrieved names RDF, JSON-LD, OWL, SHACL or SPARQL. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(d) requires DPP data to rest on open standards, use an interoperable format and be, as appropriate, machine-readable, structured, searchable and transferable over an open interoperable network without vendor lock-in; Art. 11 point (a) requires full technical, semantic and organisational interoperability between passports. Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(5) sets the same open-standard, machine-readable, structured and searchable demands for the battery passport, and Art. 78 point (a) requires semantic interoperability with ecodesign passports. Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 comes closest to this family: Art. 2(8) defines a semantic repository of data models, vocabularies and the associated ontology; Art. 2(12) defines semantic conformity as completeness, structural and value-type conformance including controlled vocabularies, and consistent interpretation by reference to the repository; Art. 8(7)(a) makes the registry check semantic conformity automatically on submission; Art. 11(3)-(4) requires passport data to follow common, versioned data models; Art. 12(2)-(3) requires typed and resolvable links, multilingual labels and DCAT-AP metadata. The act names no serialization, shape language or hash algorithm. A linked-data implementation therefore satisfies the law only if its graph also conforms to whatever data models the Commission semantic repository publishes; that repository was not located in this session.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Every node in the passport graph is named by an absolute IRI (JSON-LD '@id', often aliased to 'id') or is a blank node. Typical patterns: (1) the product IRI is an HTTP(S) URI that the data carrier encodes, for example a GS1 Digital Link of the form https://<host>/01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>, so the identifier is also the lookup address; (2) separate nodes for the product and for the passport record, linked by an object property (CIRPASS-2 battery examples link the battery node to its passport node with eudpp:hasDPP and model identifiers as their own nodes typed by the IDENT module); (3) model-level semantics named by URNs, e.g. SAMM element URNs of the form urn:samm:<namespace>:<version>#<element>, and ECLASS IRDI strings used as semantic identifiers of properties. JSON-LD resolves a relative '@id' against the document base (the retrieval URL unless '@base' or the 'base' option overrides it), and the RDF conversion drops statements whose subject or object is not a well-formed IRI. Ontologies themselves are identified by persistent w3id.org IRIs (CIRPASS-2) or vendor namespaces (https://ref.gs1.org/voc/, with owl:equivalentClass links to https://gs1.org/voc/ and https://www.gs1.org/voc/ variants).

L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: Law requires a persistent unique product identifier connected through a data carrier (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(a)-(b); Annex III) and globally unique, verifiable identifiers (Art. 12). It does not require that the identifier be an IRI that dereferences; linked data adds that expectation and adds IRIs for every attribute and code value.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: Transport is plain HTTP(S) GET on the IRI. (1) Media-type negotiation: Accept: application/ld+json, optionally with a profile parameter (JSON-LD registers http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#expanded, #compacted, #flattened, #frame, #framed and #context); Accept: text/turtle or application/n-quads; Accept: text/html for people. (2) A server that returns plain application/json or another +json type can attach the context with an HTTP Link header rel='http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#context'; more than one such header is an error ('multiple context link headers'); the header is ignored for application/ld+json and HTML. (3) An HTML page can embed <script type='application/ld+json'> or point to JSON-LD with Link rel='alternate' type='application/ld+json'. (4) JSON-LD documentUrl follows redirects except 303 See Other, which matters when a product IRI answers 303 to a data document. (5) Contexts are loaded through a documentLoader callback (LoadDocumentOptions: extractAllScripts, profile, requestProfile; RemoteDocument: contentType, contextUrl, document, documentUrl, profile); a context request asks for the http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#context profile. (6) GS1-conformant resolvers return a linkset as application/linkset+json (RFC 9264), also for application/json, JSON-LD on explicit request, HTML for people; linkType=<type> redirects to a typed link, linkType=linkset returns the set, and /.well-known/gs1resolver describes the resolver; the GS1 Web Vocabulary 1.16 defines gs1:dpp as a link type for a passport link. (7) Profile negotiation (Accept-Profile, Link rel='profile', query arguments _profile and _mediatype) is a Working Draft. (8) Solid servers must answer GET for text/turtle and application/ld+json on RDF resources they created. (9) SPARQL endpoints are a common variant; the SPARQL protocol was not retrieved in this session.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: Read is HTTP GET. Write operations depend on the variant: LDP 1.0 requires GET, HEAD and OPTIONS on resources and defines POST to containers (Accept-Post on OPTIONS), PUT with ETag and If-Match (412 on mismatch, 428 when the precondition is missing) and PATCH (Accept-Patch); containers advertise Link rel='type' with ldp:BasicContainer, DirectContainer or IndirectContainer. Solid requires GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH and DELETE, and N3 Patch bodies (text/n3) listed in Accept-Patch. Linked Web Storage 1.0 (Working Draft) defines containers, operations, notifications and a JSON-LD context. Project services expose ordinary REST APIs: the CIRPASS-2 dpp-validator has POST /validate/v1 (auto-matching by @type, @context URI or vocabulary), POST /validate/v1/{name}/{version}, and /resource/v1/... to upload, search, get and delete JSON Schemas and SHACL templates. Search is SPARQL (variant, not retrieved) or a REST search. Deactivation is usually a status property in the graph (CIRPASS-2 CORE carries a passport status property on dpp:DPP) rather than an HTTP delete.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.law_delta: Law requires data to be searchable and specifies who may create or update which data in delegated acts (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 9(2)(g)-(h), Art. 10(1)(d)). It defines no API. The registry act provides its own user interface and API (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(6)) which this family does not define.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: This is the core of the family. (A) Syntax: JSON-LD 1.1 documents with '@context' (string URL, array, or inline object). Contexts may declare '@version': 1.1, '@protected': true (terms cannot be redefined; redefinition raises 'protected term redefinition'), '@vocab', '@import', property- and type-scoped contexts. Processing mode defaults to json-ld-1.1. (B) Graph production: expansion maps keys to IRIs; in RDF conversion, statements whose subject, predicate or object is not a well-formed IRI are dropped, so a JSON key without an IRI mapping yields no triple and no error (the toRdf rule was read; the corresponding expansion step was not read). In RDF conversion a JSON number with a non-zero fraction (or magnitude of 1e21 or more) gets the canonical xsd:double lexical form and type xsd:double; integral numbers become xsd:integer; a coerced '@type' such as xsd:decimal is kept while the lexical form is still the double form (a reading of the algorithm steps, not tested here); booleans become xsd:boolean. (C) Vocabularies: CIRPASS-2 EU DPP CORE 2.0.7 (https://w3id.org/eudpp/ with modules P_DPP, ACTOR, IDENT, MAT, SOC, COMP, EVENT, LCA, CONNECTOR) and sector ontologies (battery 0.4.0 DRAFT under https://w3id.org/eudpp/battery#, tyre, textile); GS1 Web Vocabulary 1.16 (https://ref.gs1.org/voc/, gs1:Product declared skos:exactMatch schema:Product and owl:equivalentClass to the gs1.org/voc variants; 63 lines of the Turtle file mention gs1:linkType); schema.org 30.1; UNTP 0.7.0 context (protected terms); QUDT units (http://qudt.org/vocab/unit) and UN/CEFACT Rec 20 unit codes (SAMM's unit catalogue is based on Rec 20 by design decision); ECLASS IRDIs; SKOS concept schemes for closed code lists (e.g. battery categories and statuses); DCAT/DCAT-AP for catalogue metadata. (D) Constraints: SHACL Core shapes (targets, property paths, sh:datatype, sh:minCount/maxCount, sh:in, sh:pattern, sh:closed, sh:not, logical components) and optionally SHACL-SPARQL; the report is sh:ValidationReport with sh:conforms and sh:result items carrying sh:focusNode, sh:resultPath, sh:value, sh:sourceShape, sh:sourceConstraintComponent, sh:resultMessage and sh:resultSeverity (sh:Violation default, sh:Warning, sh:Info). SHACL does not require RDFS inference; sh:entailment can request a regime and a processor that lacks it must fail. CIRPASS-2 battery shapes include a profile (battery-shapes.ttl, carbon-footprint shapes with sh:deactivated items) and three tier views (public, legitimate-interest, authorities) where withheld paths carry sh:maxCount 0. (E) SAMM variant: aspect models in Turtle using urn:samm:org.eclipse.esmf.samm:meta-model:<version># with characteristics, entities and units; samm-cli 'aspect to' generates json, jsonld, schema (JSON Schema), openapi, asyncapi, aas, sql, html, java and more; Battery Pass v1.2.0 ships per aspect a Turtle model, a JSON-LD serialization of the model (-ld.json), a draft-04 JSON Schema carrying x-samm-aspect-model-urn, a sample payload and OpenAPI. Instance payloads carry no @context. (F) LinkML variant: CE-RISE model.yaml with prefixes (including gs1: https://ref.gs1.org/voc/ and an EU country authority table) and remote, tag-pinned imports, generating JSON Schema, OWL and SHACL; the hex-core-service reads a catalog with schema_url, shacl_url, owl_url and openapi_url per model version. (G) Three validation levels: syntactic validation checks the JSON tree against JSON Schema (structure, types, required keys) and is blind to meaning; semantic validation expands to RDF with the declared contexts and checks the graph against SHACL shapes, so it judges IRIs, datatypes, classes, cardinalities over the graph and is sensitive to context content; rule validation (the engine's data.rules) evaluates versioned rule packs on JSON values (completeness, units, ranges, relationships, freshness) with exact decimals and applicability conditions, and can express cross-field and applicability logic that neither JSON Schema nor SHACL Core states simply.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.law_delta: Law requires open standards, interoperable format, machine-readable and structured data (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(d); Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(5)), full semantic interoperability (Art. 11(a); Art. 78(a)) and conformance with common versioned models in the Commission semantic repository (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 11(3)-(4)). L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Passport graphs live in document stores that serve JSON-LD, in RDF triplestores (often with named graphs per passport version) or in LDP/Solid pods. Project services keep their validation artifacts in relational databases (CIRPASS-2 dpp-validator stores JSON Schemas and SHACL templates with name, version and context URI in PostgreSQL; CE-RISE dp-storage-jsondb stores DPP records as JSON). A family-specific persistence need is that the vocabularies and contexts a passport references stay resolvable for the passport lifetime; CIRPASS-2 uses w3id.org persistent IRIs, GS1 hosts at ref.gs1.org, UNECE at vocabulary.uncefact.org. Ontologies declare owl:versionIRI so old versions can stay addressable.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Two distinct mechanisms. (1) Enforcement: Solid uses Solid-OIDC for authentication and Web Access Control and/or Access Control Policy for authorization; Linked Web Storage drafts define authentication, authorization and access requests and grants; project services use OpenID Connect bearer tokens with roles (CIRPASS-2: admin, eo, eu). Research adds ODRL-based policies and UMA on Solid. (2) Specification and test of tiered views: CIRPASS-2 battery access tiers are a SKOS scheme (batacc:Public, batacc:LegitimateInterest, batacc:Authorities) derived from Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77, and three SHACL view files state what each view must carry and must not disclose; non-disclosure is written as property shapes with sh:maxCount 0 on restricted paths (33 such constraints counted in the public view). The README states that SHACL enforces nothing: the service decides, and the shapes are the specification and the test.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Integrity in this family attaches to the graph, not the bytes. RDF Dataset Canonicalization (RDFC-1.0) labels blank nodes deterministically and serializes canonical N-Quads; SHA-256 is the default hash and SHA-384 must also be supported; implementations must stop early on poison graphs. VC Data Integrity proofs (properties proof, type, cryptosuite, verificationMethod, proofPurpose, proofValue, created, previousProof) use RDFC-1.0 in the *-rdfc-* suites (e.g. ecdsa-rdfc-2019) and JCS (RFC 8785) in the *-jcs-* suites (eddsa-jcs-2022). Because the graph depends on the contexts, a changed remote context changes the canonical form and breaks the proof; JSON-LD 1.1 has no subresource integrity for contexts and advises vetting and caching. For PyLD, RDFC-1.0 and a maxPermutations work limit appear only under the unreleased 4.0.0 in the CHANGELOG; the tagged 3.3.0 source accepts URDNA2015 and URGNA2012 and defaults to the legacy URGNA2012, so a caller that does not name the algorithm gets a non-RDFC canonical form. The registry proof of registration contains a hash of the passport version without naming the algorithm (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 2(16), Art. 9(2)).

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.law_delta: ESPR foresees implementing acts on digital credentials of actors (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 11, fourth subparagraph) and requires accurate, complete and up-to-date data (Art. 9(1)); no signature format is named. Graph-level canonicalization is an addition of this family.

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: The EU registry act is the main place where semantics become a legal check: on submission the Commission reads the passport content and automatically confirms semantic conformity, data coherence, granularity, commodity code validity and the back-up link (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(7)(a)-(e)); semantic conformity means required elements present, structure, format, value type and controlled vocabularies respected, and consistent interpretation by reference to the semantic repository (Art. 2(12)). The repository holds attribute semantics, typed and resolvable links between passports, data models and formats, metadata, role semantics and multilingual labels, with DCAT-AP metadata, search and public APIs (Art. 12). DCAT-AP 3.0.1 ships SHACL shapes and a JSON-LD context that could test such metadata. The act names no serialization. Customs aspects (commodity code) are not linked-data specific.

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: Versioning appears at three levels. (1) Vocabulary and context versions: owl:versionIRI and owl:versionInfo in ontologies (e.g. battery access tiers 0.1.0, public view 0.2.0), versioned context URLs (UNTP /0.7.0/context/), version-bearing SAMM URNs (urn:samm:io.BatteryPass.CarbonFootprint:1.2.0#), LinkML model versions with tag-pinned imports. (2) Passport record versions: a schema-version property on the passport (CIRPASS-2 dpp:dppSchemaVersion, required by the battery profile and views since P_DPP 2.1.0), a passport status property (dpp:dppStatus), links to previous and next passports (dpp:linkToPreviousDPP plus object properties added in P_DPP 2.1.0) for remanufactured or repurposed batteries, and DCAT versioning properties (previous version, has version, current version, replaces, version, version notes, status). (3) Product state: the battery status of Annex XIII point 4(c) is modelled separately (bat:hasBatteryStatus with a SKOS scheme closed by sh:in in the shapes). Updates arrive as new graph versions, named graphs, PUT/PATCH on LDP/Solid resources or new documents.

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Meaning is delegated to whoever governs the vocabulary and the context file, so governance is part of the technical contract. Observed owners and terms: CIRPASS-2 consortium (Apache-2.0, w3id.org IRIs, explicit 'not official' disclaimer); GS1 (Web Vocabulary under Apache-2.0 with GS1 IP-policy text); schema.org sponsors (CC BY-SA 3.0); QUDT (CC BY 4.0); UNECE for UNTP (no vocabulary licence stated on the landing page); ECLASS e.V. The Commission becomes the authoritative maintainer of DPP data models and semantic definitions through the semantic repository (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 12(1)). Context hosting, version policy, and licence of each context are therefore conformance-relevant inputs.

end_to_end_flows.name: Publish and resolve a JSON-LD passport via an HTTP URI with content negotiation
actors: economic operator or DPP service provider
steps: 1. The operator mints a product IRI, typically a GS1 Digital Link https://<host>/01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>, and prints it in a QR code.
2. The operator publishes a JSON-LD document whose '@id' is that IRI (or a passport IRI linked to it) and whose '@context' points to versioned contexts of the chosen vocabularies.
3. The client decodes the QR code and sends GET with Accept: application/ld+json (or receives a linkset from a GS1 resolver and follows the gs1:dpp or default link).
4. The server answers 200 with Content-Type application/ld+json, or 303 to a data document, or application/json plus a Link context header.
5. The client loads each referenced context through its document loader (ideally from a local pinned copy), expands the document and converts it to RDF.
6. The client reads, queries or merges the graph with other graphs; a person receives text/html for the same IRI.

end_to_end_flows.name: Deterministic semantic validation (operator pipeline or conformance engine)
steps: 1. Pin inputs: shapes files, ontology files used as ont_graph, every context file, processor versions (e.g. PyLD, rdflib, pySHACL), inference mode 'none', severity policy.
2. Acquire the passport document and record it.
3. Check every @context reference against the allowlist (data.context exists today).
4. Expand and convert to RDF with a frozen document loader that serves only pinned contexts and refuses others (PyLD FrozenDocumentLoader or equivalent); network access of the RDF parser is blocked.
5. Run SHACL with the pinned shapes; record sh:conforms, every result and the number of focus nodes per shape.
6. Map Violation results to fail, record Warning and Info results without failing, treat zero focus nodes for a mandatory target as blocked or fail rather than pass.
7. Store the canonical form (RDFC-1.0 N-Quads) of the data graph and of the report so a replay can compare them.

end_to_end_flows.name: Tiered views checked with SHACL view shapes (CIRPASS-2 battery pattern)
steps: 1. The service holds one full battery graph.
2. For each audience it returns a filtered view after authentication.
3. The tester validates each returned view against the matching view file alone (not together with the full profile).
4. A sh:maxCount 0 violation on a restricted path shows a leak; a minCount violation shows a missing entitled field.

end_to_end_flows.name: SAMM model-first passport (Battery Pass v1.2.0 pattern)
steps: 1. The model author writes an aspect model in Turtle with SAMM meta-model namespaces and units.
2. samm-cli validates the model against the SAMM shapes and generates JSON Schema, OpenAPI, sample payloads and a JSON-LD serialization of the model.
3. The operator serves plain JSON payloads that validate against the generated JSON Schema; the semantic link is the aspect URN (x-samm-aspect-model-urn) or an AAS semanticId.
4. A consumer that wants RDF must map the payload to the model itself; no instance-level @context is provided.

end_to_end_flows.name: Registry registration with a semantic conformity check (EU law)
steps: 1. The operator submits the passport registration through the registry interface or API (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(6)).

2. The registry reads the passport content and automatically checks semantic conformity against the applicable common data model, data coherence, granularity, commodity code and back-up link (Art. 8(7)).
3. On success it issues a unique persistent registration identifier (Art. 8(8)-(10)); the operator can download a sealed proof with a hash of the passport version (Art. 9).

end_to_end_flows.name: Pod-hosted passport (Solid / Linked Web Storage, specification level only)
steps: 1. The operator stores the passport as an RDF resource in a pod container.
2. Clients authenticate with Solid-OIDC; the server enforces WAC or ACP rules per resource.
3. Public parts are readable without authentication as text/turtle or application/ld+json; updates use PUT or N3 Patch.
4. No DPP prototype of this flow was located; the flow is assembled from the Solid Protocol 0.11.0 only.

failure_modes.fault: The passport references an unversioned remote context that the publisher later edits; the same JSON now yields a different graph.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Allowlist of exact versioned context URLs (data.context) plus digest-pinned local copies; replay with the pinned copy shows a different graph than the publisher's current one only if the SUT-hosted context is recorded.

failure_modes.fault: A key is misspelled or not in the context, so expansion drops it and the attribute silently disappears for every RDF consumer while JSON Schema still passes.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare JSON keys with expanded properties (data.jsonld_dropped_terms); SHACL minCount fails on the missing path.

failure_modes.fault: Fractional values are sent as JSON numbers, so they become xsd:double (or an ill-typed xsd:decimal under coercion) and fail decimal-typed shapes or lose precision.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Datatype-fidelity finding after toRdf; SHACL sh:datatype violations.

failure_modes.fault: The product is typed with a namespace variant (https://gs1.org/voc/Product instead of https://ref.gs1.org/voc/Product, or http versus https schema.org) so shapes that target one IRI select no focus node and report conformance.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Focus-node coverage check per mandatory shape; vocabulary term check against pinned files.

failure_modes.fault: A document redefines a protected term from an included context, which a JSON-LD 1.1 processor rejects but a lax consumer accepts with a different meaning.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Expansion with a conformant processor reports 'protected term redefinition'.

failure_modes.fault: Validation results differ between runs or tools because inference, owl:imports or processor version differ (e.g. PyLD before and after 3.2.0 numeric changes).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Pin processor versions and options in the evidence record; replay comparison of canonical report.

failure_modes.fault: The server ignores Accept and always returns HTML, or returns application/json without a context Link header, so clients get no linked data.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Content-Type and Link header checks on recorded responses for each Accept value.

failure_modes.fault: JSON-LD and Turtle representations of the same IRI drift apart because they are generated by different code paths.
failure_modes.detectable_by: RDFC-1.0 canonical comparison of the two graphs.

failure_modes.fault: The passport uses a relative '@id' or a blank node, so its identity depends on the retrieval URL or is not dereferenceable, and the subject does not match the carrier URI.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Absolute-IRI check on subjects after expansion; identifier.consistency with JSON-LD id handling.

failure_modes.fault: A restricted attribute leaks into the public view under a nested path or an equivalent property that the JSON field list does not cover.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Validate the public response graph against public view shapes with sh:maxCount 0 on restricted paths; closed shapes for the public view.

failure_modes.fault: A Data Integrity proof made over a graph built with one context version fails after the context host changes the context, or verifies only because the verifier fetched the changed context.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Verify with pinned contexts only; record the context digests used.

failure_modes.fault: The schema-version label on the passport says one model version while the context URL and the shape set belong to another.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Cross-check schema-version value, context URL version and shape owl:versionIRI in persistence.versions or a rule pack.

failure_modes.fault: The passport conforms to a project ontology but not to the Commission repository model version that applies, so registration is refused on semantic conformity.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Pre-check against a pinned snapshot of the repository model once available.

failure_modes.fault: A vocabulary or context host disappears or changes domain during the passport lifetime, so consumers can no longer interpret the passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Scheduled acquisition of referenced contexts (persistence.scheduled, interface_only) with recorded status codes.

failure_modes.fault: The passport embeds licensed dictionary content (e.g. ECLASS definitions) or non-commercial model content beyond the licence terms.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Manual review of embedded definitions and licence statements; not decidable automatically.

failure_modes.fault: Producer and verifier canonicalize with different algorithms (for example PyLD 3.3.0 default URGNA2012 versus RDFC-1.0), so a hash or proof over the graph fails although the data is unchanged.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Record the canonicalization algorithm in evidence; recompute with RDFC-1.0 named explicitly and compare with the published hash; flag proofs whose cryptosuite implies RDFC-1.0 when the hash only matches under URGNA2012.

failure_modes.fault: A passport kept in a triplestore is validated through a SPARQL endpoint with a different graph scope (default graph versus named graph union) than the published document, so the endpoint result and the document result differ.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Validate the acquired published document with pinned shapes, not the endpoint; compare canonical N-Quads of the document graph with an endpoint CONSTRUCT result recorded as an artifact.

JSON-LD, RDF, SHACL, OWL and JSON Schema are not named. EUR-Lex /eng returned empty content to the fetch tool.

open_questions: Where and in what format will the Commission semantic repository of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 12 publish its data models (OWL, SHACL, JSON Schema, JSON-LD contexts)? It was not located; the conformance engine's L05 and L09 oracles depend on it.

data.context checks body contexts only. Should it also read the Link-header context of JSON responses and the targets of @import inside allowed contexts? This needs a change to the data adapter (not owned by this task).

identifier.consistency reads the key 'id' only (src/dppce/adapters/identifier.py). A JSON-LD passport that uses '@id' without an alias will look like a missing id. Should the check accept '@id' or an IXIT-declared alias? Contract change to report, not made here.

Architecture section 2 rule 5 forbids fetching any JSON-LD context. How should the engine detect drift of a SUT-hosted context? One option: acquire the context through the Acquirer as part of the SUT, record it, and compare its digest with the pinned copy. This needs a contract decision.

Which JSON-LD processor should data.shacl use? rdflib's parser loads contexts from the network by default; PyLD offers a FrozenDocumentLoader; graphs can differ between PyLD versions (3.2.0 changed number handling). The capability needs a pinned processor and version.
